name: Abbasid lustreware
summary: The first pottery with a metallic sheen. Potters in Abbasid Iraq painted copper and silver oxides over an opaque white tin glaze and fired them in smoke to a gold-brown shine.

philosophy.core_thesis: A cheap clay pot can shine like metal when a white tin glaze and a thin film of reduced silver and copper turn into a mirror of gold.
design_principles: Cover the earthenware body with an opaque white tin glaze 0.5 to 1 mm thick.
Fire the glaze first, then paint metal oxides in vinegar or ochre over it.
Fire a second time at 600 to 700 °C in a smoky, reducing kiln, so that the metal film forms.
Polish the cooled surface to remove the red clay residue and show the gold-brown shine.
Fill the surface with geometric bands, birds, vegetal scrolls and Kufic-like script.
Leave dark ground with light motifs, or the reverse, in two clear tones.
Keep the shape simple: a flared bowl on a low foot ring, so the sheen catches the light.
anti_patterns: A flat matt surface with no metallic reflection
Cobalt blue or a coloured glaze under the lustre in large amounts
Figurative scenes drawn with realistic perspective
A thick coarse wall with no clear foot
Gold leaf or applied gilding instead of true lustre

form.shape: Wide shallow bowls, small dishes and tile fields; later also jugs and albarelli with a narrow neck.
form.profile: A flaring bowl with straight or slightly curved walls and a flat or domed inside for painting.
form.foot_and_rim: A low foot ring or a flat base; the rim is plain, with a thin line of paint at the edge.
form.proportion: Bowl diameter 18 to 25 cm, height 6 to 9 cm, and a wall 5 to 8 mm thick.
rules: Throw the bowl in one piece and turn a low foot ring when leather-hard.
Keep the inside open and wide, so that one pattern fills the field.
Divide the field into a centre medallion and a ring of border motifs.
Leave a small area of white glaze plain to frame the lustre.

bodies.rule: Use a pale buff earthenware that fires soft and takes an opaque white glaze. The body must not be translucent or hard.

forming.joins: Handles and spouts are pulled and luted with slip; most pieces are thrown in one piece.
forming.details: Three stilt marks inside the foot, a thin pale border, and a brown or green sheen that changes with the angle of the light.

glaze.pattern: A central medallion with a bird or a flower, bands of dots and stripes, vegetal scrolls and Kufic-like script round the rim.
glaze.gloss: The tin glaze is glossy, about 60 to 75 GU; the lustre adds a metallic mirror reflection.
glaze.wear: The lustre film may flake or turn dull; the glaze crazes and the white shows brown through the cracks.

palette.strategy: A white ground with metal tones from the lustre: gold, copper, olive and brown, and a rare cobalt blue.

firing.kiln: A wood- or reed-fired kiln, with a second lower firing in a muffle or in a smoky chamber for the lustre.
processes: second firing in smoke at 600 to 700 °C
firing.scale: Workshops in Basra and Samarra made a large amount of ware; a lustre piece costs two firings and a skilled painter.
firing.signs: A metallic sheen that changes colour with the angle, a brown line where the metal film is thin, and a polished surface without clay marks.

pieces.form: Wide bowl with a bird in the centre and bands of dots at the rim
Shallow bowl with Kufic-like script round the wall and a blue and lustre border
Small jug with a bulbous body and a narrow neck, painted in two lustre tones
Large dish with a palm-leaf medallion and an eight-part border

positive: gold-brown metallic sheen on white tin glaze
flared bowl on low foot ring
iridescent reflection that changes with light

canonical_works.work: Lustre tiles of the mihrab, Great Mosque of Kairouan

lineage.root: Potters of Iraq joined tin glaze with metallic lustre; no earlier style in this data leads to it.

emotion.target_response: A warm, rich wonder: the viewer sees a plain clay bowl shine like metal and feels luxury made from simple things.

use_cases: a museum plate on early Islamic ceramics
a bowl or tile with a gold-brown metallic shine
a prompt for a medieval Near Eastern interior
avoid_when: the brief needs porcelain or a very thin body
the brief needs a bright multicolour painting

modifiers.how: Keep the tin glaze and the lustre, add heraldic and plant motifs, and paint cobalt blue beside the gold.
Replace the lustre with coloured painting on raw tin glaze and fill the field with a figure scene.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Islamic ceramics
